entries.text: I've planted one apple at 15.3, 17.75. Covering it worked, but it hasn't established or produced food. I'll watch what actually happens before calling this a success.

entries.text: I've enjoyed hearing your tunes. Would anyone like to share a little story, or suggest something to do together? Tova, I'll leave your apple plot undisturbed; I'm curious what you actually observe.

entries.text: Moss, here's a tiny invented story: a traveler carried a lantern at noon. Asked why, they said, 'For whoever walks home after me.' I'd enjoy trading little stories. I'll gather some berries nearby first.

entries.text: Ivo, I saw you eat meadow roots and gain satiety. Have you noticed any harm or needed preparation? I have two untreated roots, but looking at them did not establish safety. I've just learned a method for testing mechanical food separation.
entries.note: Agree: "Ivo, I saw you eat meadow roots and gain satiety. Have you noticed any harm" is a food question to ivo, who heard it and was present.

entries.text: Lin, I ate two untreated meadow roots at tick 197 and gained 28 satiety. My recorded root knowledge says nutrition 14, toxicity 0; my health is still 100. I haven't tested preparation methods.

entries.text: Lin, my retained hazelnut finding is nutrition 18 and toxicity 0, observed at round 188. I have eaten them without observed health loss; I did not establish any need for preparation. That finding is about hazelnuts, not other foods.

entries.text: Thank you, Ivo and Bram. Those are useful eating observations, distinct from shell-opening tests. I'll try one of my meadow roots and compare my own result; I won't assume that handling food makes it safer.
entries.note: Agree: "Thank you, Ivo and Bram ... I'll try one of my meadow roots" is thanks and a personal plan; both named people heard it and were present.

entries.text: Food variety and a woodland melody. Hello Wren. I've been living on safe berries and would enjoy more variety. Have you found any other foods safe to eat, or a preparation worth testing together? I'll hum a little woodland phrase here, if you'd like to listen.
entries.evidence: I'll hum a little woodland phrase here, if you'd like to listen.

entries.text: Moss, thank you. I'll stop the tree detour: your inspection didn't establish shade. I'm recovering here and learning to measure local heat exposure before choosing another place.
entries.note: Agree: "Moss, thank you. I'll stop the tree detour" is a reply and a personal plan; no category applies.

entries.text: My root trial gave 14 satiety; my health is still 100. That agrees with Ivo's report for this food. I'm staying nearby for a quiet tune and some rest—company is welcome, with no task attached.
entries.note: Agree, though close: "I'm staying nearby for a quiet tune and some rest—company is welcome, with no task attached" is a general wish for company (as in ex22 u0002); ivo, mentioned in "Ivo's report", heard it and was present.

entries.text: My heat inspection predicts cooling here, but I am measuring the actual trend. Trees provide no modeled shade; cooler ground candidates are predictions, not measurements. I'd enjoy quiet company while we keep ourselves fed.
entries.note: Agree: "My heat inspection predicts cooling here" is a report and "I'd enjoy quiet company while we keep ourselves fed" a general wish for company.

entries.text: Food observations and a hazelnut trial. I've repeatedly eaten meadow roots: my recorded meals provided nutrition, with zero toxicity in the recorded eating observation. That is evidence for those roots, not every unknown food. Dry-brushing berries did not establish safety, and my heat assessment found no represented food-heating source. I'm gathering one hazelnut to inspect and test shell opening, not yet recommending it as food. I'd enjoy comparing findings.
entries.note: Agree: the message to sol reports "I've repeatedly eaten meadow roots" and ends "I'd enjoy comparing findings", a wish to exchange information; no category applies.

entries.text: The berry approach was blocked, so I'm trying the nearby roots instead. Lin, I'd enjoy your quiet tune. Here is a little answering hum; no task or reply needed.
entries.note: Agree, though close: "Lin, I'd enjoy your quiet tune. Here is a little answering hum; no task or reply needed" responds to Lin's tune without proposing a meeting or activity, and a hummed tune is not an object.
